tier_rationale: Both the manufacturer's product page and its instruction manual describe browning as controlled by a wind-up mechanical timer rather than a numbered electronic setting, with a mechanical selector switch for slot count and a manual ejector knob for Peek & Pop. The manual lists replaceable elements, couplings and the timer itself as user-serviceable parts and contains no app, WiFi, or digital-control feature across 24 pages.
the_unplug_test: You push the lever down, the wind-up timer dial ticks backward, and the toast pops when it reaches zero. You can check progress any time by pushing the ejector knob down and letting go (Peek & Pop) without cancelling the cycle. Unplugging and replugging changes nothing about how it behaves next time, because the only memory in the device is the mechanical position of the timer dial.

repairability.notes: Manufacturer sells spare parts directly, including replacement ProHeat heating elements and replacement timers, and states the toaster is hand-assembled in the UK with the assembler's name on the base plate. Dualit markets the line explicitly as 'Fully Repairable'.

sources.supports: Manufacturer product page for the 2 Slice NewGen Classic Toaster: 'Browning is controlled by a mechanical timer rather than a conventional numbered setting... The patented ProHeat elements are replaceable, as are other working parts including the timer.' Describes the selector switch and Peek & Pop ejector as mechanical controls. No app, WiFi, or connectivity feature mentioned anywhere on the page.

Dualit's own Vario Toaster (2/3/4 slot) Instruction Manual, which covers the same mechanical-timer control architecture used on the NewGen Classic: illustrated wind-up timer dial with browning levels 1.5-2.5, mechanical slot selector, manual ejector/Peek & Pop knob, and a defrost setting operated by winding the timer to a symbol and back. No digital display or connectivity feature appears in the 24-page manual.

open_questions: The manufacturer page (dualit.com) is the UK storefront (GBP pricing); US availability and price were corroborated via Williams-Sonoma's US site rather than a US-specific Dualit page. Worth confirming the US-market unit (120V, UL/ETL listing) uses an identical timer mechanism rather than a region-specific control revision.
notes: Dualit's home/countertop 'Classic' line, distinct from its NewGen electronic-touch toasters if any exist in other Dualit ranges; this record covers only the mechanical-timer NewGen Classic. Sold in numerous colors under different SKUs (27180-27512 etc.); all share the same mechanical control architecture per the manufacturer page, so the color choice does not change the tier.
